subject: Reserved deployment sizing: HorizonAI P1 - tokens/sec, SLO fit, and headroom
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Subject: Reserved deployment sizing: HorizonAI P1 - tokens/sec, SLO fit, and headroom

Hi Cal,

Thanks again for walking through the P1 requirements this morning. Below is a concise sizing recommendation for the reserved (dedicated) deployment you asked for — focused on tokens/sec, p95 latency fit, and operational headroom so you can move forward with procurement. Spreadsheet attached with the detailed calculator.

Summary (ask: 250k tokens/sec sustained peak, 400ms p95 latency target for typical completions):
- Model family: redwood-compat/70B-q4 (production variant used in the PoC).
- Typical completion profile used for sizing: prompt 120 tokens, completion 280 tokens (avg total 400 tokens).
- Observed single-GPU throughput (we measured on H100-like nodes for this model): ~600 tokens/sec (steady-state) at 400ms p95 for short bursts; A100-80GB expected ~320 tokens/sec for same workload.

Sizing math (baseline):
- Required pure throughput = 250,000 tokens/sec / 600 tok/s per H100 = 417 GPUs (if only using GPUs for all traffic).
- Apply production headroom factor (1.5x) for burst tolerance and maintenance windows => ~625 H100-equivalent GPUs.
- KV/prefix caching expected to reduce steady-state GPU load by ~20% for Horizon's traffic pattern (heavy reuse across sessions) => effective GPUs after cache: ~500 H100-equivalents.
- Fallback plan: maintain smaller pool of lower-cost quantized 70B instances (q4_0) for best-effort traffic and graceful degradation. These can absorb lower-fidelity, high-volume requests and reduce H100 pressure in 10-20% peak windows.

Options and cost/ops tradeoffs (high level):
1) H100 reserved pool (recommended for strict p95 target): ~500 H100-equivalent GPUs reserved. This keeps p95 at or under 400ms with KV caching and gives operational headroom.
2) Mixed pool (recommended if budget constrained): 350 H100-equivalents + 150 A100-equivalents + aggressive caching and batching. Expected p95 risk ~+10-20% under highest tail.
3) Commitment phasing: start with 300 H100-equivalents as an initial commit + burst credits (60%) for first 90 days while we tune cache/warmup. Ramp to target over three quarters.

Notes / risks:
- Tail latency is sensitive to cold KV loads and long contexts (we assumed ~400-token average). If you expect longer completions often, we should re-run the model with 1k-token profiles.
- Quantization and kernel selection can improve per-GPU throughput; we will include recommendations in the attached spreadsheet.

Next steps:
- Marissa, can you review the ops/sla implications below and confirm whether Horizon needs on-prem isolation or VPC private deployment?
- Cal, if these numbers look directionally okay, I can hand this to procurement with a phased commitment proposal and a draft MSA.

Attachments: horizon_reserved_sizing_v2.xlsx (sizing calculator), horizon_poc_latency_profile.csv (measured traces), MSA-HorizonAI-draft.pdf

Thanks,
Karthik

Karthik — good summary, thanks. Quick ops/engineering caveats:

On Tue, Sep 12, 2027 at 09:15 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> (original message)

- The 20% caching reduction estimate is contingent on Horizon's session stickiness and prompt reuse. Those numbers came from samples in the PoC but we need a 7-day window of production traces to validate. If reuse is lower, GPU requirement increases by ~30%.
- Cold-start KV warmup: our measurements show p95 jumps ~2.2x for the first 60s of a cold cache; recommend a small pre-warmed standby pool equal to ~5-7% of baseline GPUs to keep tails in check. For the recommended 500-equivalent count, that means ~30–35 GPUs pre-warmed.
- Maintenance/resizing: suggest automated staged ramping (canary pools) to avoid large p95 regressions during weekly kernel updates.

Operational recommendation (concrete):
- Initial commit: 360 H100-equivalents reserved + 45 pre-warmed standby (10% margin). Parallel: enable aggressive KV caching TTLs and a 7-day telemetry collection period. After 30 days, re-run the spreadsheet; plan for a 2-week window to add capacity if traces indicate lower reuse.

Irene — if Horizon confirms VPC private deployment (they mentioned compliance constraints), we'll need to size for the network egress and offer a private control-plane plan. I left the draft MSA with the privacy clause tracked (see attached PDF).

Marissa
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Karthik — appreciate the level of detail. A few clarifying questions before we present to our VP of infra:

1) Can you produce two concrete flavor quotes: (A) conservative (360 H100 + 45 pre-warmed) and (B) target (500 H100-equivalents after cache)? Include a 12-month committed rate and burst credit pricing.
2) For the mixed pool option, what p95 delta should we expect in real terms (ms) for common queries?
3) Can you confirm whether the deployment model supports keeping the control plane in our VPC? That is a hard requirement for our procurement team.

If possible let's lock a 30-minute sync tomorrow 09:00 PT with Marissa and Irene to walk the pricing impact. Procurement is looped.

—Cal

Subject: Re: Reserved deployment sizing: HorizonAI P1 - tokens/sec, SLO fit, and headroom

Cal — thanks. See attached updated sizing workbook (v2) with two pricing flavors and an executive summary. Highlights:

- Conservative (A): 360 H100-equivalents reserved + 45 pre-warm (10% standby). Estimated committed monthly cost: USD 2.1M/month. Burst credits available at 60% of base capacity for an additional usage fee. Expected p95 under typical load: ~380–420ms.
- Target (B): 500 H100-equivalents reserved (post-caching). Estimated committed monthly cost: USD 2.9M/month. This keeps p95 comfortably under 400ms with 1.5x headroom for non-cacheable peaks.
- Mixed pool delta: 350 H100 + 150 A100 (cost optimized) — expected p95 increase ~+80–120ms on median tail for heavy inference; acceptable for background/async workloads but not for low-latency customer-facing flows.

Control plane: yes — we support a private-control-plane option (VPC peering + customer-managed keys). We'll add the clause into the MSA; Irene included a tracked change.

DocuSign: I attached a redlined MSA and a link to a preliminary SOW/commitment which you can review: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1zHorizon-MSA-draft

Meeting: 2027-09-13 09:00 PT works for me. I will bring pricing and an ops runbook.

Attachments: horizon_reserved_sizing_v2.xlsx, MSA-HorizonAI-draft.pdf

Best,
Karthik
